title: Rung Down
summary: Since sunset the Cambridge Quarters have played three phrases of four. Somebody has pulled the pins out of the tune.

intro.line: Above the market the quarter chime begins: four notes, four more, four more... and then nothing, where the last phrase should be.

steps.text: Find Absalom Crane on the steps of Great St Mary's

dialogue.line: You'll be Nell's Warden. You have the look: singed, and a bit surprised to be alive.
We are rung down, Warden. Rung right down. Hear that? Three phrases of the Quarters, and then a hole where the fourth should be.
Is that the Unwinder again?
Corvin. Yes. I taught that boy to ring. Now he's pulled the tune-pins from my chime barrel and flung them across the parish.
First things first. Something has come down out of the louvres and is roosting in my churchyard. Clear it, would you?

steps.text: Clear the creatures roosting by the tower

dialogue.line: Bats made of bell-rope and soot. He's turned my own tower against me. There are four pins: one for each phrase.
The first phrase always carried towards the Senate House. Start there, and listen for brass humming in the wrong key.

steps.text: Find the first tune-pin by the Senate House railings

dialogue.line: A brass pin as long as your hand lies against the railings, humming four falling notes.
Far up the street towards Trinity, something answers with the second phrase.

steps.text: Follow the second phrase up Trinity Street

dialogue.line: The second pin is wedged between two setts, warm as a coin held in a fist.
Behind you, from the stone frontages of King's Parade, the third phrase rings out. It sounds frightened.

steps.text: Recover the third tune-pin on King's Parade

dialogue.line: The third pin lies in the gutter of King's Parade, its notes slowed almost to a growl.
The last phrase is the lowest, and it comes from the narrow lane of Bene't Street, near the oldest tower in town.

steps.text: Find the fourth tune-pin in Bene't Street

dialogue.line: Four pins, four phrases. Held together they almost play the whole tune.
Almost. From the foot of Great St Mary's tower comes the sound of a bell-rope being hauled by something that is not a ringer.

steps.text: Defeat the Chime-keeper of St Mary's at the foot of the tower

intro.line: The Chime-keeper of St Mary's steps out of the tower's shadow: a walking belfry, its clock hands spinning, striking in fours.
Count its strokes, Warden! One-two-three-four, then it draws breath. Hit it in the breath!

dialogue.line: The Chime-keeper's hands stop at the quarter. It sets itself down at the tower foot, and is only stone again.
From high above, all four phrases of the Quarters ring out over Market Hill, complete for the first time since sunset.
Listen to that. Every phrase in its place. You've no idea how a man misses a tune until it's gone.
The Concord is twelve bells, Warden: one for each hour, from my tower out to the edge of the town. Together they hold the Undertide down.
And the thirteenth chime?
That's no bell of ours. Each time Corvin silences one of the twelve, the thirteenth rings a little louder. When it can strike on its own, the river comes up through the streets.
Take these. Ringer's sallies, my own. And go and see the Sister in Bene't Street. The Saxon bell's been ringing flat, and that bell is older than all of us.
